clue.text: Was he in EastEnders? Familiar bloke longing to return

parts.note: 'old cock' is a familiar British way of addressing a man

indicators.note: asks for the word for longing to come back the other way

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a TV soap character, followed by a man pining to come home.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, but here it means people born in the East End; 'to return' reverses the longing word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner born within sound of Bow Bells, traditionally an East End resident, is exactly an EastEnder.

clue.text: Tea drinking in tea-producing country

indicators.note: something drinking another takes it inside, so the tea word swallows the next word

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea

explanation.surface: A tea-producing nation where tea is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is one of the world's biggest growers of tea, so it fits as a tea-producing nation.

clue.text: Give us a ring about love that's heartless

indicators.note: the phone phrase goes around the love letter, sitting about it

parts.note: to give someone a ring is to phone, so ring us is call us
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone who won't even phone with affection is cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: CALL US surrounds O to give CALL-O-US.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous behaviour shows no feeling or sympathy, the same as being without a heart.

clue.text: Not glorious, not good and out of line

definitions.text: Not glorious, not good and out of line

indicators.note: says the line letter is to leave what remains as well
says the good letter is to be absent from the first two words

explanation.surface: A description of someone disreputable: inglorious, bad and badly behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: From NOTGLORIOUS remove G ('not good') and then L ('out of line'). The whole clue also describes being infamous.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous for something bad, the opposite of glorious fame, and the whole clue sketches such a person.

clue.text: Annual that's soon after end of May

indicators.note: places the soon word after that final letter
takes the final letter of the month's name

parts.note: early can mean soon, before long

explanation.surface: A plant or event that comes around shortly after May finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual happens once each year, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: "Right height? Yes. 1 Down?" might do — for something rather like this clue

parts.note: the porcelain or country at 1 Down suggests Ming, the dynasty famous for fine porcelain

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue, whose opening words chime with each other, asking what it resembles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right height' rhymes, which is the definition's point: this clue sounds like verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's opening pair chime, so the clue itself behaves like verse with matching end sounds.

clue.text: If resistance weakens is this why? Flawed hero's rubbish

definitions.text: If resistance weakens is this why?

indicators.note: something flawed is faulty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A man of heroic resistance breaks down, and the result is junk.
explanation.definitionFit: This device varies electrical resistance in a circuit, so it is the reason a resistance would drop.

clue.text: Enclosures for animals, say — they all have three feet

definitions.meaning: stockyards and farmyards are fenced spaces for livestock
an imperial measure of length equal to three feet, plural

explanation.surface: Animal pens that, oddly, are all three-legged.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm pens are called this, and each imperial unit of the same name measures exactly three feet.

clue.text: The opposite of 5Ac? …

definitions.meaning: a mathematical or logical reverse or converse
a clue that chimes like poetry is written as poetry, split into two words

explanation.surface: A question asking what the reverse of a rhyme might be.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN VERSE, the answer describes what rhymes are written in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a reversal or converse, and split in two it describes poetry, where chiming lines belong.

clue.text: … or take a look at the dear attachment to Albert?

parts.note: the dear stuff, the expensive precious metal
to watch is to look at

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue: take a look at the precious thing hung on a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: An Albert is a Victorian pocket-watch chain named after Prince Albert. Following the 'opposite' idea of the previous clue, the look word and the dear word are entered in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket timepiece hangs from an Albert chain, so an expensive one is attached to it, traditionally a retirement gift.

clue.text: Will knocked off early with a rib that's uncomfortable

indicators.note: the first letter of the name is knocked away

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Will left work early and, being teased, felt awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes feeling awkward or uneasy, the same as being uncomfortable.

clue.text: Coming with a right for knockout in match

indicators.note: the pair is there to be knocked out of the coming word

parts.note: an arrival is a coming
A plus R, the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A boxer arriving with a right hook to knock out his opponent in a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To equal or match someone's achievement is to rival it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Following a procedure, united Romeo and his Juliet?

definitions.text: Following a procedure, united Romeo and his Juliet?

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of procedure
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Following a set routine, Romeo was joined with his Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' only links; the whole clue also pictures the love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, especially a secret one, is what joined the famous pair of Verona lovers.

clue.text: Salt sprinkled around verrucas — that does it with this

indicators.note: salt is scattered, so its letters land in a new order
turns the warts word round

parts.note: verrucas are warts, on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone putting salt on their verrucas, a remedy that finally ends things.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT rearranges to LAST; WARTS read backwards gives STRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final burden that makes something unbearable, the moment one says enough is enough.

clue.text: From this road you get a chance across the board

definitions.text: From this road you get a chance across the board

parts.words: From this road you get a chance across the board
parts.note: on the London Monopoly board, the light-blue road of this name sits beside a Chance square

explanation.surface: A road that seems to offer an all-round opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly's London board has a Chance square next to this road; 'across the board' means on the board, not universally.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street of this name is a property on the British Monopoly board, close to a Chance card space.

clue.text: They make trunk calls as new telephone is vandalised after one's cut off

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked, so the letters are mixed up
the letters spelling one are cut from the end of the phone word

parts.note: the word one, spelt out

explanation.surface: A new phone box wrecked after its line was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ONE from TELEPHONE leaves TELEPH; with AS and N, those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These animals trumpet through their trunks, and a trunk call is an old British term for a long-distance phone call.

clue.text: A flashy bird and a libertine going into caress

indicators.note: puts the libertine pair inside the caress word

parts.note: to pet is to stroke or caress
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker

explanation.surface: A showy man about town and a rake going in for a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly coloured small parrot is a vividly plumed, showy bird.

clue.text: Stiff condition of e.g. canvas — this rip almost repaired

parts.note: a painted canvas is an example of art

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together differently, so the letters are reordered
the rip word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A torn canvas, nearly mended, is in a stiff state.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP less its end gives RI; THIS plus RI rearranges to HRITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This joint disease causes stiffness and pain, so it is a stiff medical condition.

clue.text: Caught hiding in small space in place of Queen's prosecutor?

indicators.note: the caught letter hides within the rest

parts.note: an en is a small printing space, half an em
for can mean instead of, in place of
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal caught hiding in a cramped room instead of facing the royal prosecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of space, half an em, which is why it can be a 'small space'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who imposes compliance or pursues offenders acts loosely as a prosecutor, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Making cuts and relieving of duty

definitions.meaning: cutting out, as a surgeon removes tissue
read as ..., freeing from excise duty, a tax

explanation.surface: Cutting staff and dismissing them from their posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cutting out; split cryptically, it means taking excise tax away, a punning second sense.

clue.text: Ring artist for a wild fancy

parts.note: to chime is to ring
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Phoning a painter on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the mythical beast, the word means an illusion or fanciful wild notion.

clue.text: Maybe tack on a bit of savings by the little guy

indicators.note: places the little-guy word next to that letter
takes just the opening letter of savings

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A small saver adds a little to his savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a long loose temporary stitch in sewing, so it is one example.

clue.text: Concerning split in peace pact rout

indicators.note: the concerning word is broken up, its letters scattered through the pact word in a new order

parts.note: on can mean concerning, about
a truce is a ceasefire agreement

explanation.surface: A disagreement breaks a peace deal and leads to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' reads as the concerning word's two letters being broken apart and scattered through the pact, so the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce an opponent is to beat them heavily, a verb synonym for routing them.

clue.text: It's not over for the vicar's helper

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: turns the following small word over, back to front

explanation.surface: A parish worker who isn't finished yet.
explanation.definitionFit: This church officer looks after the building and graveyard, assisting the parish priest.

clue.text: This alone might be part of a fall and a freeze

definitions.text: part of a fall and a freeze

indicators.note: says the letters could become something else

explanation.surface: A lone item that could be part of a tumble and a cold snap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice is one piece of a downpour of frozen precipitation.

clue.text: Quickly rising part of flight going over Spain

indicators.note: the stair word goes over, covering, the Spain letter

parts.note: a step is one stair in a flight
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A stair, part of a flight of steps leading over Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that climbs sharply rises quickly, which is what a steep hill does.

clue.text: Origins of racial or other traditional systems

definitions.text: Origins of racial or other traditional systems

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An inquiry into where ethnic and other customs come from.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sources or ancestry, which the whole clue describes as where traditions began.

clue.text: A bit of artless language

indicators.note: the answer is one stretch within the two words

explanation.surface: A snatch of unsophisticated speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal unpolished vocabulary is exactly artless language, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Relative from a French city say?

indicators.note: says the city name is pronounced to give a different spelling

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A relative who comes from a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's daughter is a family relative.

clue.text: Intelligence comprehends very fast? Pathological inertia results

indicators.note: comprehends here means includes, takes in

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
at a ton is British slang for at 100 mph, very fast

explanation.surface: Clever spies grasp speed, while a sickly sluggishness follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical state of stupor and immobility is a pathological form of inertia.

clue.text: A mark for every run

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
per means for each

explanation.surface: A scoring mark awarded for each run in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for running away, bolting off quickly.

clue.text: Something put by e.g. Gents if going round the bend

indicators.note: going mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something stashed by in the men's lavatory, say, if it goes round the bend of the pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings set aside for the future are something put by, an idiom for reserved money.
